description: Bounded edge-insertion profile for the min-max-angle triangulation objective on convex triangles and quadrilaterals.

source.title: Optimal Triangulation
source.author: Tiow-Seng Tan
source.algorithm_paper: H. Edelsbrunner, T. S. Tan, and R. Waupotitsch, An O(n^2 log n) Time Algorithm for the Minmax Angle Triangulation, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 13(4), 994-1008 (1992), DOI 10.1137/0913058
source.copyright: The chapter and paper are copyrighted publications; this package uses the algorithm description and objective only.

input.vertex_order: strict convex boundary order, clockwise or counterclockwise; no three points collinear

output.meaning: 1-based rank of the optimum maximum angle among distinct angles from every 3-point subset; rank equals one plus the number of distinct smaller angle measures

algorithm_details.primary: Start from the 0-2 fan triangulation. Select a largest-angle triangle, then scan all tied largest-angle occurrences in deterministic triangle/vertex order. For each occurrence, test the unique remaining point s; insert q-s only when it properly crosses the triangle's opposite edge. The insertion replaces the two fan triangles, and is accepted only if the replacement's maximum angle is strictly smaller. N<=4 makes this a bounded instance of the paper's edge-insertion step.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Enumerate the single triangle for N=3 or both triangulations for N=4, directly evaluate each triangulation's maximum angle, and choose the smaller objective.
algorithm_details.exact_angle_order: For vectors u and v, compare the sign of dot(u,v) first; when signs agree, compare dot(u,v)^2 divided by (u.u)*(v.v) with integer cross products. No trigonometric or floating-point comparisons are used.
algorithm_details.tie_rules: Visit the fan triangles in listed order and their sorted vertex indices in ascending order; retain the first equal maximum angle. Scan all occurrences tied at that angle. Keep the fan on equal objective values. The result rank collapses equal angle measures across triples.
algorithm_details.primary_complexity: O(A^2) time and O(A) scratch for A=3*choose(N,3)<=12 angle values; fixed N<=4.
algorithm_details.oracle_complexity: At most two triangulations, each with N-2 triangles, plus O(A^2) exact angle-rank work; fixed N<=4.
